To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a mathematical model of the first part of the Wnt signaling pathway and validated it with experimental data from two independent published studies.
a validated mathematical model of Wnt signalling predicts a synergistic effect of sFRP and Dickkopf (Dkk) on Wnt-induced beta-catenin accumulation.

we developed a new mathematical model of the initial sequence of Wnt pathway events and validated it by accurately predicting the effect of Wnt ligand and two inhibitors (sFRP1 and Dickkopf-1) on β-catenins levels in different experimental systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new mathematical model of the initial events of the Wnt pathway that is capable of accurately predicting the effects, both individually and in combination, of two inhibitors of this pathway.
the development of an in silico model of the Wnts pathway and its use to predict the efficacy of different inhibitors.

the development of a mathematical model of the early events in the WNT signalling pathway, which is validated with experimental data and predicts the synergistic effect of two different inhibitors of the pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is a good tool for predicting the effects of inhibitors on β-catanin levels, and it is a good starting point for the design of new experiments to test its predictions.
the model is able to predict the effect of sFRP and/or Dkk on Wnt-induced beta-catenin accumulation.
the model is a useful tool to predict and understand the effects of inhibitors of the Wnt pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a validated mathematical model can help in predicting the outcome of combinational therapy in a disease.
the mathematical model of the canonical Wnt signalling pathway is able to predict the effects of Wnts and their inhibitors on β-cataenin levels in different experimental conditions.
a validated mathematical model was developed to describe the initial sequence of the events in the WNT signaling pathway, from ligands binding to beta-catenin accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mathematical modelling is a useful tool to identify novel therapeutic strategies.
the model can be used to identify potential targets for intervention and predict the effect of different treatments.

a simple mathematical model of the early events in the WNT signalling pathway is sufficient to predict the effects of sFRP and Dickkopf inhibitors on β-catanin levels in different cell types and to identify a new treatment avenue based on a combination therapy.
